# Reviewed Pine engine sources

EdgeLab pins PineTS 0.11.0 under AGPL-3.0-only. The original npm package stays unchanged. `scripts/pine-engine.mjs` reconstructs its exact readable sources from the packaged browser source map and applies the reviewed files in `overrides/`. The missing, type-only Indicator barrel comes from the pinned package's declaration re-exports.

`manifest.json` seals the installed version, source-map bytes, declaration barrel, original source bytes and each modified file with SHA-256. Development and production workers use the same source resolver. A changed dependency or patch fails the build until its source and hashes are reviewed together. Imports resolve only to the verified sources and three bundled MIT dependencies; there is no network fetch or arbitrary disk fallback.

The local changes preserve `varip` declarations and object-field metadata, and provide an explicit indicator-only realtime lifecycle for deterministic engine tests. Compiler-generated type metadata retains the upstream type registry and correct method receiver name, including overloaded methods. Ordinary mutable values roll back between updates; intrabar-persistent values and fields retain their appropriate state. Provisional outputs replace the current bar. `setRealtimeMode(true)` is required before `run`; `updateTail(context, { confirmed: false })` recalculates an open bar and `{ confirmed: true }` closes it. Provider bars must remain chronological. Streaming, paginated realtime and strategy tick scheduling are unsupported and fail explicitly.

The primary Binance Live chart uses this lifecycle through a persistent isolated worker per visible native indicator. Other feeds, editor runs and Replay use closed snapshots. `{ received: true }` explicitly executes an accepted provider event even when its OHLCV is unchanged; omitting that flag preserves the engine's unchanged-update shortcut. This integration does not establish TradingView parity. Tests cover supported scalar, collection and declared UDT field rollback, moving-average state and provisional output replacement. Full drawing-object behavior and per-tick performance budgets are not established. Member and type-factory UDT copies use current declared fields, preserve absent/undefined values, and retain shallow references to collections and other objects. See `backend/tests/pine-object-copy55.test.js` for copying tests, `pine-realtime54.test.js` for actual minified-engine lifecycle tests and `pine-engine-integrity54.test.js` for build integrity tests.

Historical object-field receivers are lowered as values in plotting arguments and function returns. Pine v6 uses `(object[offset]).field`; direct field history on registered UDT receivers is rejected with a corrective diagnostic. Pine v5 and JavaScript inputs retain their existing compatibility paths. `backend/tests/pine-object-history56.test.js` verifies existing historical receivers, custom offsets, copied and nested objects, reference identity, typed methods and explicit realtime lifecycle updates. First-bar field access through an absent object is not established by these tests.

Explicit realtime sessions can initialize an entirely closed dataset with `setRealtimeMode(true, { initialTail: "historical" })`. Those bars execute once as confirmed history; the next explicit appended bar starts realtime execution. The default `initialTail: "open"` retains the provisional final-bar behavior.

Realtime rollback state has hard limits of 16,384 mutable nodes, 262,144 mutable cells and 1,280,000 Series slots. Trusted callers may select smaller positive integer limits through `limits: { nodes, cells, seriesSlots }`. Exceeding a limit raises `REALTIME_STATE_LIMIT` and halts that session. Discarded newborn rollback records are released after restoration while historical references, aliases and surviving intrabar state remain available. These are snapshot-state limits, not a total heap or execution-time guarantee: scripts and the underlying engine can allocate memory before snapshot checks. `backend/tests/pine-realtime57.test.js` covers retention, limits and closed-history initialization. `pine-live58.test.js` exercises the genuine minified worker's persistent command protocol, received events, explicit closes, fresh packed buffers and session failures.

Field-level intrabar persistence follows the [Pine objects documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/objects/): a persistent object reference does not exempt its ordinary fields from rollback. Excluding discarded newborn field qualifiers from persistence discovery is a local retention policy; TradingView equivalence for discarded-object aliases is not established.

Historical strategy fill recalculation accepts strict boolean `calc_on_order_fills` declarations, including resolved constant and input aliases. The local broker visits open, the nearer extreme, the farther extreme and close in order, executes eligible fills, and awaits the script after each actual fill. Historical callbacks see the final bar OHLCV; newly created orders only use the remaining price path. It preserves one history/output slot per candle, rolls back ordinary script state between executions, and retains the broker ledger and supported `varip` state. The [TradingView execution model](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/language/execution-model/) and [strategy documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/#calc_on_order_fills) define the historical fill contract; these tests do not establish complete TradingView equivalence or actual tick-history accuracy.

`backend/tests/pine-strategy65.test.js` checks the actual minified worker's four-fill reversal ledger, brackets created after entries, remaining-path execution, rollback/history, multi-lot partial exits, cancellation/replacement, close timing, fees and slippage. Fill recalculation refuses intrabar margin liquidation with `UNSUPPORTED_ORDER_FILL_CONTEXT`; historical-tick recalculation and lower-timeframe bar magnification remain unavailable. Each candle has hard limits of 512 script calculations and 2,048 broker transitions (`STRATEGY_EXECUTION_LIMIT`). Historical rollback uses the existing bounded snapshot graph; the limits do not cover total heap allocation. Live strategies retain their explicit refusal. Omitted/false fill settings retain the original single-calculation broker path.

Explicit `qty_percent=100` unscoped exits use the complete available quantity and persist for subsequent entries until flat. They preserve reservations and normal cancellation/replacement behavior; scoped exits do not attach to entries created after the exit call’s bar and a positive fixed `qty` still takes precedence. Partial percentages and fixed quantities are allocated independently per physical entry when fill recalculation is enabled. The reviewed `cancel_all.ts` override follows the [TradingView cancellation contract](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/#strategycancel-and-strategycancel_all): it removes all unfilled entry and exit orders, including pending market closes, without closing filled positions. The minified-worker matrix in `backend/tests/pine-strategy68.test.js` and production sandbox gate `e2e/pine-strategy68.config.ts` cover these behaviors, including the retained single-calculation path.

Historical trailing exits support absolute or entry-relative activation and offsets in instrument ticks. Activation changes broker state without running Pine; an actual fill triggers the configured recalculation. Each physical entry lot retains its own favorable peak, updated only at prices visited after the order exists. Pending replacements preserve that lot's armed state; cancellation, removal of the trailing component and a fresh position retire it. Pine v6 selects the activation reached first when both levels are supplied, while v5 prioritizes the absolute level. Optional `na` arguments are absent; an all-`na` exit disables its previous generation and creates no market close. Malformed distances fail explicitly. Ordinary closed-bar strategies also fill an already armed opening-gap stop at the open before later price-path targets. Incomplete trailing components alongside a valid fixed exit use the fixed exit as a qualified local policy. These are tested historical OHLC semantics, not proof of every TradingView replacement/tie case or live scheduling. See `backend/tests/pine-strategy66.test.js` and `e2e/pine-strategy66.config.ts`.

Modified files retain the original LuxAlgo copyright and AGPL notices, with an EdgeLab modification notice. Matching source distributions must include these overrides, manifest, build script and the locked dependency sources. See the repository licence and third-party notices.

With historical `calc_on_order_fills=true`, fixed or partial-percentage exit generations retain per-entry reservations across later fills. An exhausted generation cannot consume the same lot's remainder automatically; an unscoped generation can cover later lots until flat. Scoped exits retain matching pending entries created before or on the call's bar, even when they fill later. Percentages use each original entry size, and a positive fixed quantity takes precedence. Cancellation/replacement releases the previous generation's reservations. Quantity tolerances follow the supplied increment, so valid `1e-10` quantities and partial remainders are not treated as flat. The shared independent ledgers in `backend/tests/fixtures/pine-strategy70.mjs` run through the actual minified worker and `e2e/pine-strategy70.config.ts` production sandbox gate. This implements the separate-entry model described by [TradingView's strategies documentation](https://www.tradingview.com/pine-script-docs/concepts/strategies/#exits-for-multiple-entries); fixed-quantity multi-entry sizing is inferred from that model rather than a recorded TradingView comparison. The original single-calculation broker path remains separate, and broader parity is unproven. FIFO closed-trade accounting can differ from the physical lot that supplied an exit price. Live strategy scheduling, bar magnification and intrabar liquidation with fill recalculation remain unavailable.

Input activation metadata preserves earlier input references and constant aliases as bounded expression data. The host resolves it against validated current values for Check/run and settings controls, without running Pine source on the UI thread. Reviewed overrides are `inputs/analyzeInputs.ts` and `Indicator/scanInputs.ts`; unsupported expressions fail explicitly. The expression protocol permits literals, input references, unary arithmetic/not, logical/comparison/arithmetic operators and ternaries, with at most 64 nodes and depth 7.

Enum input analysis resolves constant aliases through lexical scope, with cycle/persistence/reassignment guards and a maximum alias chain of 256. Each declared member is an immutable, nonplain token interned within its full execution context; field titles are separate display data. The worker bridge uses versioned exact member IDs with declared labels and bounded member lists. Duplicate titles retain distinct comparison, history, array and map-key identity. `str.tostring()` explicitly returns the title, while direct enum arguments to `str.format()` are rejected. The original Pine AST checks enum declarations, assignments, equality comparisons, supported functions/methods, switch branches and collection operations before lowering, including unreachable branches and compatible overloaded calls. This pass rejects recursive functions and bounds inference to 100,000 expression visits and 64 nested calls. These checks do not establish full qualifier inference, all built-in signatures or UDT field typing. Enum method dispatch matches receiver and declared enum argument identities, preserving untyped argument positions. An unresolved `na` or missing argument that matches multiple enum overloads raises an explicit ambiguity error; compile-time-only identity through such values is not implemented. Type checking does not repair the upstream distinct-body ordinary-function overload dispatch path. The existing unsupported nested-binary historical UDT field path remains separate. See `pine-enum-runtime93.test.js`, `pine-enum-types93.test.js` and `pine-enum-protocol93.test.js` for actual minified-engine and bridge coverage.
